sentences.1: Whoso would be a man must be a nonconformist.
sentences.2: He who would gather immortal palms must not be hindered by the name of goodness, but must explore if it be goodness.
sentences.3: Nothing is at last sacred but the integrity of your own mind.
sentences.4: Absolve you to yourself, and you shall have the suffrage of the world.
sentences.5: No law can be sacred to me but that of my nature.
sentences.6: Good and bad are but names very readily transferable to that or this; the only right is what is after my constitution, the only wrong what is against it.
sentences.7: A man is to carry himself in the presence of all opposition, as if everything were titular and ephemeral but he.
sentences.8: I am ashamed to think how easily we capitulate to badges and names, to large societies and dead institutions.
sentences.9: Every decent and well-spoken individual affects and sways me more than is right.
sentences.10: I ought to go upright and vital, and speak the rude truth in all ways.

leftover: Sentence 1: “Whoso would be a man must be a nonconformist.” — Would and must make a normative/aspirational condition. No actual man or actual nonconformity is asserted.

Sentence 2: “He who would gather immortal palms must not be hindered by the name of goodness, but must explore if it be goodness.” — Desire, obligation, immortal-palms image and the embedded goodness question have no asserted nonmodal result. No LETS/STOPS tendency is inferred from hindered.
Sentence 3: “at last” — Temporal/ultimate emphasis is not checked.

Sentence 4: “Absolve you to yourself, and you shall have the suffrage of the world.” — An imperative followed by a promised social response. The imperative is mentioned, not a claimed action; suffrage of the world is figurative total approval. No actual approval or executed plan is claimed.

Sentence 5: “No law can be sacred to me but that of my nature.” — Modal can be sacred to me, together with first-person valuation and the nature-law image. It is not an actual universal denial of other laws' sanctity.
Sentence 6: “but; very readily transferable to that or this” — Rhetorical limitation and ease of reassignment are outside scope. No specific reassignment is asserted.

Sentence 7: “A man is to carry himself in the presence of all opposition, as if everything were titular and ephemeral but he.” — Normative is to and as-if comparison. No actual opposition event or literal claim that everything else is ephemeral is asserted.

Sentence 8: “I am ashamed to think how easily; capitulate; large; dead institutions” — Mental attitude, ease and size, and capitulation/death imagery. i retains the presupposed social yielding as one free description, without physical surrender or biological death.
Sentence 9: “more than is right” — Comparative excess and normative standard are not checked; no degree of influence is encoded.

Sentence 10: “I ought to go upright and vital, and speak the rude truth in all ways.” — Ought marks a duty rather than an action; upright/vital has evaluative imagery, and in all ways is unbounded manner. No speech event is asserted.

readings: Sentence 3. Open readings: integrity is the only sacred thing or a merely necessary condition for sacredness. Chosen: retain the positive valuation a and a marked only-ways reading b; own_mental_integrity is not silently equated with another moral property.
Sentence 6. Open readings: right/wrong as definitions or only necessary conditions. Chosen: definition-like sufficiency plus explicit only-ways necessity, without equating wrong with NOT right.
Sentence 8. Open readings: literal military capitulation or social deference. Chosen: social yielding, filled in; no physical pressure class guessed.
Sentence 9. Open readings: a habit with exceptions or categorical every. Chosen: ALWAYS; SHOWS chosen for the descriptive generic. No particular decent individual is invented.
